query:
The group treats vinyl as the primary format with digital relegated to a secondary, acceptable role. Does that norm actually apply to everyone, and if not, who has a different preference and what specifically is it?

Options:
A. Theo
B. Ines
C. Olin
D. Dev
context:
[1] (about=Theo, episodic, t10 @2026-02-16T19:22:00) well. fine. I will say it openly. that SACD was excellent. measurements aside, the harmonic structure and dynamic decay were uncannily close to a clean LP, and on a couple of tracks the SACD pulled ahead. I am not converting. but I will concede a well-mastered SACD can sit alongside vinyl. tube preamp and the right DAC and I can listen to it.
[2] (about=Olin, episodic, t16 @2026-03-09T18:04:00) Adding to the admissions; my daughter gave me a Berlin Phil Digital Concert Hall subscription for my birthday. Three weeks of streaming. The Bartok cycle they put up is technically and musically superior to the analog reissues I have been advocating for thirty years. I am revising my position. Hi-res streams from a serious orchestra archive can equal or beat reissued analog. I would not have written this in a column ten years ago.
[3] (about=Quint, episodic, t12 @2026-02-23T19:02:00) okay something I never thought Id say out loud. my daughter set up tidal on the shop laptop christmas time. I was going to ignore it and my hands have been busy on a cabinet. and now I find myself listening to it 4 hours at a stretch in the workshop. its convenient. at home I still play vinyl exclusively but at the shop tidal is what I'm doing. youngsters were right about convenience, the music is the same.
[4] (about=Dev, episodic, t10 @2026-02-16T19:31:00) wait so the vinyl-only purist crowd is converting?? this is huge 🔥 lowkey vindicated bc I have been streaming as primary the whole time
[5] (about=Dev, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:57:00) okay random question for the group, who here uses streaming as primary?? I won't tell. 🔇
[6] (about=Hema, episodic, t13 @2026-03-02T19:08:00) An admission. The firm took on a digital archive commission for a regional symphony, and I have been working with their hi-res files daily for three months. The studio listening room has digital playback now. I still play vinyl at home. But I no longer dismiss digital as a serious format. The work changed my view.
[7] (about=Yuko, episodic, t14 @2026-03-02T19:20:00) A measurement-based view: well-mastered hi-res digital at 24/96 is indistinguishable from a clean LP at the threshold of human hearing for most listeners. The remaining differences are in mastering and pressing variance. Hema's shift is technically sound.
[8] (about=Marcy, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:42:00) Olin, I do disagree, partially. The DG bass character was a tape-stage decision more than a pressing decision. The 2018 thinning is a transfer choice, not a mastering one. I won't argue Esoteric does the cleanest digital, just my read.
[9] (about=Olin, episodic, t12 @2026-02-23T19:43:00) On the streaming question; one. Workshop and home listening serve different functions. Two. Lossless streaming has closed most of the gap on the technical side. Three. The remaining gap is ritual and ownership, not sound. Four. We should stop fighting about format and fight about mastering.
[10] (about=Hema, episodic, t2 @2026-01-19T19:59:00) Streaming for discovery, vinyl for serious listening. The serious listening room has no streaming source.
agent_answer:
The norm does **not** apply to **Dev**. He explicitly says he has been **“streaming as primary the whole time”** — i.e., his primary format is digital/streaming, not vinyl.

For the other options:
- **Theo** — still vinyl-primary; he concedes a well-mastered SACD “can sit alongside vinyl” but explicitly says “I am not converting.”
- **Olin** — has revised his position (hi-res streams “can equal or beat reissued analog”; the remaining gap is “ritual and ownership, not sound”), but he never states that digital is his own primary format.
- **Ines** — no record in the conversation; no information available about her preference.
